My hypothesis is that 922 is a invasive phonomenon that affects far beyond its description.

It expands its affection range whenever a person has realized its existence and started to be aware of such phenomenon.

While the civilian don't even know and not being affected, the Foundation has done a good job spreading 922 among themselves, the review done by site-305 and Site-11 is how it all started.

To me, the biggest creepiness comes from the letter sent by Dr.Marlowe to the O5.

What if Dr.Marlowe is created by SCP-922!? and the letter was also an engagement to affect the O5s?
DOES THE PERSON THAT HAS BEEN CREATED BY SCP-922 EVEN KNOWS THEMSELVES ARE MADE UP???

Addendum1: Being such a invasive and effective phenomenon, 922 doesn't seem to be hostile or harmful to human, and it does provide experienced and well trusted personnels for the Foundation, thats why I think its not a Keter but Euclid

item.content:encoded: I love the complex layers of this one. Others have called it redundant, but without that redundancy, it simply would not be as effective. The progressive reveal is very effective at creating that sense of confusion and unease and never quite knowing what the reality is. It's like "waking up" from a dream to find you're in another dream. And the utter lack of a resolution makes it just that much better. Given the liberal use of amnestics and other techniques by the foundation, it's quite plausible that someone who is actually a site director could be thoroughly forgotten like that.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This works so well on so many levels. I found myself wondering if it wasn't Dixieland Nightmare Magic, mostly because of the citation footnote. (Though the redacted location really should have disabused me of that notion.)

I mean, on the one hand, you've got the nightmare of all nightmares of college registration (which I've never experienced myself, but I've heard stories). Then you've got a phenomenon that should by all rights be Keter, and I have a feeling it's not just because they can't verify anything one way or another. All the high-level secrets stuff keeps things interesting, and good on you for making an inter-Foundational research citation actually be narratively important! (Not to mention I'm really intrigued by "The Inconsistent Carbo Family".)

The more you think about this, the more you realize we can't do shit about it. Sure, those people were confirmed to be working here X years ago, but what if they were created longer ago than that? What if the Director is fucking with the results? It's like, holy shit, this could be one of the worst containment breaches in Foundation history, and we can't even know for sure. Fantastic.
